items.followUp: What digits are used in the binary number system, and what is its base?

rubric.why: Identifies the base of the binary number system.
rubric.description: States that binary is a base-2 number system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its base is 2.

rubric.why: Identifies both digits used in binary.
rubric.description: States that binary uses only the digits 0 and 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both digits are given.

modelAnswer: The binary number system is a base-2 number system.
It uses only the digits 0 and 1.

items.followUp: What does the AND operator do when one or both of its inputs are false?

rubric.why: Explains the condition under which OR produces a true result.
rubric.description: States that OR gives true when at least one input is true.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the true-output condition.

rubric.why: Identifies the condition under which OR produces a false result.
rubric.description: States that OR gives false only when both inputs are false.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the false-output condition.

modelAnswer: The OR operator is a logical operator that gives a true result if either or both inputs are true.
It gives a false result only when both inputs are false.

items.followUp: Describe file sharing on a network and give one example.

rubric.why: Explains what application sharing allows users to do.
rubric.description: States that users on a network can access or use a shared application.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing application sharing.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of application sharing.
rubric.description: Gives a relevant example, such as users working on a shared spreadsheet or using a video-conferencing application.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example.

modelAnswer: Application sharing allows users on a network to access or use the same application.
For example, several users can work on a shared spreadsheet.
